newsitem.title: UK: North Sea crudes steady at lower levels, thin.
newsitem.headline: North Sea crudes steady at lower levels, thin.

text.p: North Sea crudes were holding steady at the lower levels in quiet trade on Friday afternoon.
Traders said, the market had largely shrugged off news of higher December loading programmes with thinner supply of late November cargoes supporting the wet Brent market.
Wet Brent traded at 48 cents under December or the equivalent of 16 cents under January, which is unchanged from previous trade on Thursday.
Most of the remaining Nov Brent was held by Statoil which was believed to be taking the barrels transatlantic.

Supplies of other North Sea grades were limited to a couple of Statfjord and Ekofisk cargoes, the last remaining Oseberg having sold late on Thursday at a relatively healthy Dated Brent plus 23 cents.

Next week's CFDs eased a couple of cents in early business to two cents under January and were holding this levels in late afternoon trade with the next three weeks at four cents under, four under and seven under respectively.
Despite the downward pressure on the front end of weekly CFDs, further forward monthly CFDs were better bid.
